cues.en: 787 sold as a Dreamliner. An all-new airplane in a once in a decade if not once in a generation achievement of human ingenuity. For airlines it's cheap to fly. For passengers it offers unparalleled comfort. Wow. For Boeing it promised windfall profits. The Dreamliner is the plane of the future. But Al Jazeera discovers a dark side to the Dreamliner.
cues.zh: 作为 Dreamliner 出售的 787。这是一架全新飞机，堪称十年一遇、甚至一代人一遇的人类智慧成就。对航空公司来说，它飞行成本低。对乘客来说，它提供无与伦比的舒适。哇。对 Boeing 来说，它承诺带来意外暴利。Dreamliner 是未来之机。但半岛电视台发现了 Dreamliner 的阴暗面。

cues.en: Unimaginable that we could be three years late, have a fleet grounding, have fires on the airplane. Our investigation finds Boeing altered its own quality standards. They're shortchanging the engineering process to meet a schedule. We uncover a whistle blower fired as he fought for safety. There's no doubt this bad repair is going out the door on the 787. We go behind closed doors.
cues.zh: 无法想象我们会晚三年、整个机队停飞、飞机上起火。我们的调查发现 Boeing 修改了自己的质量标准。他们为赶进度而压缩工程流程。我们揭露出一名举报人，他因争取安全而被解雇。毫无疑问，这个糟糕的维修正被装到 787 上出厂。我们走进紧闭的大门。

cues.en: onto the factory floor to reveal a world Boeing keeps secret. January 16, 2013, Takamatsu, Japan. A brand new Boeing 787 Dreamliner makes an emergency landing. Passengers knew the plane was in trouble.
cues.zh: 进入工厂车间，揭开 Boeing 秘而不宣的世界。2013年1月16日，日本高松。一架全新的 Boeing 787 Dreamliner 紧急降落。乘客知道飞机出事了。

cues.en: The blue box was one of the Dreamliner's two lithium-ion batteries.
cues.zh: 那个蓝盒子是 Dreamliner 两块锂离子电池中的一块。

cues.en: the most powerful and risky ever permitted on a commercial aircraft. It's just the latest in a string of embarrassments for Boeing's state-of-the-art aircraft. Nine days earlier, a Dreamliner battery had caught fire in Boston, Massachusetts. Two battery failures in less than two weeks. Japanese carriers all nip on Airways and Japan Airlines have grounded their fleets of Boeing 787 Dreamliners. Japan Airlines and ANA had been the first to fly the Dreamliner. Now they became the first
cues.zh: 这是商用飞机上获准使用的最强大、也最危险的电池。这只是 Boeing 最先进飞机一连串难堪事件中的最新一起。九天前，一块 Dreamliner 电池在马萨诸塞州波士顿起火。不到两周内两起电池故障。日本航司全日空和日本航空已停飞各自的 Boeing 787 Dreamliner 机队。日本航空和 ANA 曾是最先执飞 Dreamliner 的航司。现在它们成为第一批

cues.en: to cancel all flights. Breaking news, the United States Federal Aviation... Within 24 hours, the U.S. safety regulator, the Federal Aviation Administration, grounded the 787. All 50 of the new Boeing 787 Dreamliners have now been grounded. The rest of the world followed. No Boeing fleet had ever been forced from service. But on January 17, 2013, the dream was over. I'm Will Jordan.
cues.zh: 取消所有航班的航司。突发新闻，美国联邦航空……24小时内，美国安全监管机构联邦航空管理局停飞了 787。全部 50 架新型 Boeing 787 Dreamliner 现已停飞。世界其他地区纷纷效仿。此前从未有 Boeing 机队被迫停飞。但在2013年1月17日，梦想结束了。我是 Will Jordan。

cues.en: For a year, my team and I have been investigating the Dreamliner. It's the Boeing company's big bet on the future. A plane created to save fuel, improve comfort and boost profits. Built in a new way. Designed and manufactured by scores of companies around the globe. The company that makes the battery is GSUASA, based in Kyoto. We wanted them to tell us what had gone so wrong.
cues.zh: 一年来，我和团队一直在调查 Dreamliner。这是波音公司押注未来的大手笔。一款旨在节省燃油、提升舒适度并增加利润的客机。以一种全新的方式打造。由全球数十家公司联合设计制造。生产电池的公司是总部位于京都的 GSUASA。我们想让他们告诉我们，到底出了什么严重问题。

cues.en: Hi, how are you? I wonder whether you might be willing to do an interview They refused The battery is only one part of the Dreamliner's complex electrical system There's also a charger made at a factory thousands of kilometers away
cues.zh: 嗨，您好。不知您是否愿意接受采访？他们拒绝了。电池只是 Dreamliner 复杂电气系统的一部分。还有一个充电器是在数千公里外的一家工厂制造的。

cues.en: What happened there shows Boeing learnt years ago just how dangerous a lithium-ion battery could be. In Tucson, Arizona, we tracked down Michael Leon, an electrical technician. I've been working electronics since I was 17 years old and I joined the paratroopers and was assigned to an electronic communications battalion to the 82nd Airborne. Yeah, this is the first time I've been here since 2007.
cues.zh: 那里发生的事情表明，波音多年前就已深知锂离子电池有多危险。在亚利桑那州的 Tucson，我们找到了电气技师 Michael Leon。我从 17 岁起就一直在搞电子，当时我加入了伞兵，被分配到第 82 空降师的一个电子通信营。没错，这是我自 2007 年以来第一次回到这里。

cues.en: It's hard to believe that this is what's left of a three-story engineering structure. On a November morning in 2006, Leon and dozens of other workers clocked in at Securaplane, the company that makes the battery charger. And I started a pot of coffee, then I went into my lab and started working on my battery charging unit. And then it happened.
cues.zh: 很难相信，这座三层的工程建筑如今只剩这副模样。2006 年 11 月的一个早晨，Leon 和其他几十名员工照常来到生产电池充电器的 Securaplane 打卡上班。我煮了一壶咖啡，然后走进实验室，开始捣鼓我的电池充电装置。接着，事故发生了。

cues.en: And it was a very loud explosion, and all of a sudden I was lying on the floor and there it was, coming out the side of this battery, it was about that big, and it wasn't like fire, it looked like a jet afterburner, like jet exhaust. The prototype battery Secureplane was using to test its charger had exploded. I heard a very loud series of metallic rattling bangs.
cues.zh: 然后是一声巨响，我突然就躺在了地上，电池侧面喷出东西来，大概有那么大，不像火，倒像是喷气机的加力燃烧器，喷气尾流一样。Secureplane用来测试充电器的原型电池爆炸了。我听到一连串非常响亮的金属撞击声。

cues.en: and just this jet of steam. The fire was literally rolling up the walls around me and on the ceiling I could just see it eating up all around me. I know that if that happened on board an aircraft there would be no chance of survival. It was the biggest chemical fire in Tucson's history. A 10,000 square foot, three story structure burnt to the ground. After my building burned down.
cues.zh: 还有那股蒸汽喷射。火焰简直沿着我周围的墙壁往上窜，天花板上我都能看到火在四周蔓延吞噬。我知道如果这事发生在飞机上，根本没有生还的可能。这是图森史上最大的化学品火灾。一栋一万平方英尺、三层高的建筑烧成了灰烬。我的那栋楼烧毁之后。

cues.en: After that, they realized very emphatically the danger of this chemistry. Richard Luxo knows well the chemistry of the Dreamliner battery. Boeing chose the most powerful there is, but also the most volatile. They went to lithium cobalt, which is, wow, up here is fire danger. Luxo stepped down as secure plane president just before the fire. He started a new company.
cues.zh: 在那之后，他们非常强烈地意识到了这种化学物质的风险。Richard Luxo深谙梦想客机电池的化学特性。波音选了其中最强劲的，但也是最不稳定的。他们用了钴酸锂，那火灾风险，哇，高得不得了。Luxo在火灾前刚辞去Secureplane总裁的职务。他开了一家新公司。

cues.en: to make lithium-ion batteries for business jets. Luxo was a true believer in the technology. Then he began testing. Two 3.3 amp hour series battery pack bullet tests. Luxo went beyond even the latest industry guidelines, going so far as to fire bullets into batteries to see if they could be made safe for military applications. Yeah, you can run the test that you feel that you need
cues.zh: 为公务机制造锂离子电池。Luxo是这项技术的忠实信徒。然后他开始测试。两个3.3安时串联电池组的枪击测试。Luxo甚至超越了最新的行业准则，竟然向电池开枪，看能否让电池达到军用级别的安全标准。对，你可以做你认为需要的测试。

cues.en: to meet the requirements to be safe. But you also need to have a conscience that's going to tell you, I want to do the extreme. In the end, testing with a conscience, Luxo couldn't make the batteries meet the requirements. His new company failed. We became proficient in destroying batteries. And the more we learned about it, the worse it got. I mean, oh my God, we kept digging and digging.
cues.zh: 来满足安全要求。但你也得有良心告诉你，我要做到极致。最终，凭着良心做测试，Luxo无法让电池达标。他的新公司失败了。我们变得很擅长摧毁电池。而且我们了解得越多，情况就越糟。我是说，天哪，我们不停地深挖，越挖越深。

cues.en: And we were saying, I wonder what the rest of the guys were doing. Well, I guess we knew. By the rest of the guys, he means Boeing. And they were testing to a weaker standard. One written by the FAA specifically for the Dreamliner. It's the FAA's job to regulate air safety. But when it comes to building airplanes, the FAA delegates oversight almost completely to the aircraft manufacturers. When it comes to the battery and beyond, Boeing...
cues.zh: 我们当时还说，不知道其他那些人都在忙什么。嗯，我想我们是知道的。他说的“其他那些人”指的是波音。他们在按一个更宽松的标准做测试。这个标准是FAA专门为梦想客机写的。监管航空安全是FAA的职责。但一到造飞机，FAA几乎把监管权完全下放给了飞机制造商。说到电池以及更广的范围，波音……

cues.en: largely police's itself. The batteries passed Boeing's tests. In line with the FAA rules, Boeing said the 787 batteries would virtually never catch fire on board an aircraft. Then they failed twice in just nine days. Boeing has not uncovered the root cause of the failures. It found a workaround, a strong steel case, more insulation, and an exhaust for noxious fumes.
cues.zh: 基本上是自己管自己。电池通过了波音的测试。按照FAA的规定，波音称787的电池在飞机上几乎永远不会起火。结果九天内就失败了两次。波音没有查明故障的根本原因。它找到了一个变通方案：坚固的钢壳、更多绝缘材料，以及一个排放有毒气体的排气口。

cues.en: Any fire will be impossible because there's not enough oxygen to support combustion. But several leading scientists have their doubts. I don't think it's a sufficient fix. Even inside that steel box with all of its fortifications, all the elements are still there for fire. Despite not knowing the root cause, America's safety regulator, the FAA, was satisfied. And in April 2013, the Dreamliner was back.
cues.zh: 任何火灾都不可能发生，因为没有足够的氧气支持燃烧。但几位顶尖科学家对此表示怀疑。我认为这个修复并不充分。即便在那个钢箱里、有那么多加固措施，起火的所有要素依然都在。尽管不知道根本原因，美国安全监管机构FAA还是满意了。2013年4月，梦想客机复飞了。

cues.en: But this story goes far beyond a burning battery. It begins at Boeing itself. Since its creation in Seattle nearly a century ago, Boeing had developed a reputation as a world-class engineering company. But in 1997, Boeing changed. It merged with competitor McDonnell Douglas. Two companies with two very different business models.
cues.zh: 但这个故事远不止一块起火的电池。它从波音本身开始。近一个世纪前在西雅图创立以来，波音一直享有世界级工程公司的声誉。但在1997年，波音变了。它与竞争对手麦克唐纳-道格拉斯合并。两家公司，两种截然不同的商业模式。

cues.en: The merger was all about transforming our successful culture and business model into the same business model that McDonnell Douglas had used unsuccessfully. You basically shortchange engineering, you stop doing aggressive new product developments, you run the business for cash. The new Boeing moved its headquarters from Seattle, the only home the company had ever known, to Chicago. It began slashing investment in research in order to cut costs.
cues.zh: 这次合并完全是要把我们成功的文化和商业模式，变成 McDonnell Douglas 曾用过但没成功的同一种商业模式。基本上就是亏待工程部门，停止激进的新产品开发，只顾现金经营业务。新的 Boeing 把总部从西雅图——公司唯一熟悉的所在地——搬到了芝加哥。它开始大幅削减研究投资以降低成本。

cues.en: and maximise Wall Street returns. I felt it was wrong. I felt the company was going to take the company in the wrong direction, and I thought that quality would suffer and the integrity of the product would suffer. I feel that that legacy and that history and that competence has been hijacked by a bunch of corporate thugs. By 2003, it was time to launch a new plane. But Boeing's new board...
cues.zh: 并最大化华尔街回报。我觉得这是错的。我觉得公司正被带向错误方向，我认为质量会受损，产品的完整性也会受损。我觉得那份传承、那段历史和那种能力，已经被一群企业恶棍劫持了。到2003年，该推出一款新飞机了。但 Boeing 的新董事会……

cues.en: was reluctant to invest the billions needed. The board made it clear that they wanted this plan made for less money. They wanted it made for $5 billion. They wanted partners to come in to pay the rest. Expensive. So how do you make that happen? Well, you promised them that you can do it for less. And then worry about the consequences later. Boeing came up with a plan to save itself money.
cues.zh: 不愿投入所需的数十亿美元。董事会明确表示，希望这个计划少花钱。他们希望用50亿美元做成。他们希望合作伙伴进来付剩下的钱。这很烧钱。那怎么做到呢？你就向他们承诺你能少花钱做成。然后再担心后果。Boeing 想出了一个给自己省钱的计划。

cues.en: It would push the costs onto its major suppliers. Boeing would call them partners, and they would design and pay for the parts they built. Boeing's job would be to assemble the plane. It was almost as if at times you thought Boeing executives believed, well, maybe they could sit in Chicago and have other companies do things, and they would just rake in the money somehow by putting it all together and putting a Boeing sticker on it at the end.
cues.zh: 这会把成本转嫁给主要供应商。Boeing 会称他们为合作伙伴，由他们设计并支付自己制造的零件。Boeing 的工作就是组装飞机。有时你几乎会觉得，Boeing 高管真的相信：也许他们可以坐在芝加哥，让别的公司干活，最后只要把所有东西拼起来、贴上 Boeing 标签，就能轻松大赚一笔。

cues.en: Right on schedule, Boeing rolled out the Dreamliner on Sunday, July the 8th, 2007. 787. The airlines with us today have made a big commitment to Boeing and to this airplane. So far, they have ordered 677 of them. I think in a lot of ways, July 2007 was one of the more magical moments I've seen in the industry. Watching us live around the world broadcasting, I'm told in 45 countries in nine languages.
cues.zh: 波音如期在2007年7月8日星期日推出了梦想客机。787。今天在座的航空公司都对波音和这款飞机做出了重大承诺。到目前为止，他们已经订购了677架。我觉得从很多方面来说，2007年7月是我在业界见过的比较神奇的时刻之一。看着我们在全球直播，据说覆盖45个国家、9种语言。

cues.en: for the premiere of this very exciting new Boeing 787 Dreamliner. We were all inside the factory with artificial lighting. Big stage, Tom Brokaw, huge screens. Then they opened the doors of this giant assembly bay and in rolls this beautiful, beautiful aircraft. And there it is sitting in the sun and we all stream outside and we all touch it. And none of us know this.
cues.zh: 为这款激动人心的新型波音787梦想客机的首秀。我们都在工厂里，打着人造灯光。大舞台、汤姆·布罗考、巨大的屏幕。然后他们打开这个巨型装配车间的门，这架美丽绝伦的飞机就缓缓推了出来。它就停在那里晒着太阳，我们全都涌出去摸它。而我们谁都不知道。

cues.en: And I'm reassured by all the executives involved that it's going to fly within two months. One, two, three. What I realized walking around it is that you could look up in the wheel well and you could see daylight. We learned that the whole thing was a sham. Beautiful, isn't it? Absolutely beautiful. They roll out this thick airplane. I realized the doors were made of plywood. This plan that we were admiring
cues.zh: 相关高管向我保证，它两个月内就会飞。一、二、三。我绕着它走的时候意识到，你往轮舱里一看，能看到日光。我们后来才知道整件事就是个骗局。很美，对吧？绝对美。他们推出了这架厚实的飞机。我发现那些门是胶合板做的。我们欣赏的这架飞机

cues.en: was completely a shell inside. None of this would be possible, of course, without exceptional leadership. There's only two conclusions you can draw. You have executives there who are either lying, in which case they're clueless because they're going to get caught in two months, or you have a complete disconnect between the people who are working on the plane, the engineers, and the executives who are saying this. And so to each and every member of the 787 Global Team,
cues.zh: 里面完全是个空壳。当然，没有卓越的领导力，这一切都不可能实现。你只能得出两个结论。要么那里的高管在撒谎，那他们就是糊涂，因为两个月后就会被揭穿；要么就是造飞机的人、工程师和说这话的高管之间完全脱节。所以，对于787全球团队的每一位成员，

cues.en: I say thank you, congratulations, and keep up the great work. More than any other single event, it was the big lie, and it was a statement that the Boeing company is now all about the big lie. The day after the roll-out, Wall Street pushed Boeing's stock to a 10-year high. But it was all about to unravel, as revealed in Boeing's investor calls.
cues.zh: 我要说谢谢你们，恭喜你们，继续加油。比起任何其他单一事件，这就是那个弥天大谎，它宣告波音公司现在全靠弥天大谎。推出次日，华尔街就把波音股价推到了10年新高。但这一切即将崩盘，正如波音投资者电话会议所揭示的。

cues.en: Welcome to our quarterly update on the 787 program. September 2007, Boeing announces its first delay. It's not a failure how the airplane goes together. It's just a really complicated puzzle. October 2007, the three-month delay becomes six months. We wish we didn't have to do this. New kinds of innovation present challenges and we're doing our best to meet them.
cues.zh: 欢迎收看 787 项目的季度更新。2007 年 9 月，波音宣布首次延期。这不是飞机组装出了故障，只是一个极其复杂的拼图。2007 年 10 月，三个月的延期变成六个月。我们也不希望这样。新型创新会带来挑战，我们正尽力应对。

cues.en: October 2009, six months becomes two years of delays. We know that we can and must do better and I'm confident that despite our setbacks we will get the 787 through the flight test program and into the hands of our customers. It just kept getting worse and worse and it seemed unbelievable. You have to understand this was unprecedented. There'd never been a Boeing delay in a Boeing program.
cues.zh: 2009 年 10 月，六个月的延期变成两年。我们知道我们能够也必须做得更好，我相信尽管遭遇挫折，我们仍会让 787 通过飞行测试项目，交付到客户手中。情况越来越糟，简直令人难以置信。你得明白，这是前所未有的。波音项目从未出现过延期。

cues.en: The sequence of events looked an awful lot like a catastrophe rather than just a manageable series of delays. The Dreamliner business strategy was backfiring. Designed to save so much money, it was costing Boeing billions. The outsourcing plan failed very badly. All these different suppliers who were going to build these major sections couldn't actually do it. To fix the Dreamliner...
cues.zh: 这一连串事件看起来非常像一场灾难，而不只是一系列可控的延期。梦想客机的商业策略适得其反。本为节省大量资金而设计，却让波音损失数十亿美元。外包计划严重失败。所有这些原本要建造主要部件的不同供应商，实际上都做不到。为了修复梦想客机……

cues.en: Boeing dispatched hundreds of quality inspectors to struggling suppliers around the globe, including to its partner, Alenia, in southern Italy. We are just working through the final part of the process. Alenia would take on the task of constructing the body of the plane, not with aluminium panels, but with composite plastic barrels. The main objective? To lose weight, saving fuel and making the 787 cheaper to run.
cues.zh: 波音向全球陷入困境的供应商派遣了数百名质量检查员，包括位于意大利南部的合作伙伴 Alenia。我们正在完成流程的最后部分。Alenia 将承担机身建造任务，不用铝板，而用复合塑料筒体。主要目标？减轻重量，节省燃油，让 787 的运营成本更低。

cues.en: But no one had ever made anything like this before, not Boeing and especially not Alenia. There is nothing comparable with that on the market. There's nothing built like that. Boeing's quality inspectors have won overriding priority to make sure the job is done correctly. In 2009, when inspectors found flaws in parts made in this Alenia plant, they ordered work to stop. A year later, in Alenia's other factory,
cues.zh: 但此前从未有人造出过这样的东西，波音没有，尤其是阿莱尼亚也没有。市场上没有可与之相比的产品。没有像这样建造的东西。波音的质量检查员获得了最高优先权，以确保工作正确完成。2009年，当检查员发现这家阿莱尼亚工厂生产的零件存在缺陷时，他们下令停止工作。一年后，在阿莱尼亚的另一家工厂，

cues.en: They again found serious problems and again they ordered work to stop. But this time managers overruled the quality inspectors. This internal Boeing document from 2010 reveals executives ordered a linear to continue with fabrication without delay. We followed at that time the procedure to stop.
cues.zh: 他们再次发现严重问题，并再次下令停止工作。但这一次， managers 否决了质量检查员。这份2010年的波音内部文件显示，高管们下令 a linear 继续制造，不得延误。我们当时遵循了停止的程序。

cues.en: But with the help of Boeing specialists at the time, while we were in this approved condition, they took responsibility for approving the quality and we will continue to work in engineering the time, the product. In this separate memo obtained by Al Jazeera, Boeing states that schedule may require deviations to the preferred quality process. We received the memos from an engineer who, like many we spoke with, was afraid to appear on camera.
cues.zh: 但当时在波音专家的帮助下，在我们处于这一批准状态期间，他们承担了批准质量的责任，我们将继续在工程时间、产品方面工作。在半岛电视台获得的这份单独备忘录中，波音表示，日程可能要求偏离首选质量流程。我们从一位工程师那里收到了这些备忘录，他像我们交谈过的许多人一样，害怕出现在镜头前。

cues.en: so he answered my questions by email. The quality engineer told us deviating from the process compromised safety. Alenia and Boeing said it did not. So I brought the memo to the former president of Boeing's engineers union. So my name is Cynthia Cole, C-Y-N-T-H-I-A, last name's C-O-L-E. Cynthia Cole spent 32 years at the company, but never on the Dreamliner program.
cues.zh: 所以他通过电子邮件回答了我的问题。这位质量工程师告诉我们，偏离流程会危及安全。阿莱尼亚和波音表示不会。于是我把备忘录带给了波音工程师工会的前主席。我叫辛西娅·科尔，C-Y-N-T-H-I-A，姓C-O-L-E。辛西娅·科尔在这家公司工作了32年，但从未参与梦想客机项目。

cues.en: So she had never seen this memo before. The program schedule may require deviation to the preferred process. See? That one sentence right there, that one fragment of the sentence. You know, you don't change your quality process for schedule. You make quality happen in the schedule. They're short-changing the engineering process to meet a schedule.
cues.zh: 她之前从未见过这份备忘录。项目进度表可能要求偏离首选流程。看到了吗？就是那一句话，句子中的那个片段。你知道，不能为了进度而改变质量流程。你要让质量在进度中实现。他们为了赶进度而在工程流程上偷工减料。

cues.en: They're not even allowing quality control to do their job. And they're telling them, this is how it's going to be. I don't see how these people who write these things and agree to these things and the signatures down here, how they sleep at night. I just don't get it. How can you do that? As an engineer, I find that reprehensible. How does that make you feel as a flyer? Oh, yeah. Yeah, I'm not flying on a 787.
cues.zh: 他们甚至不让质量控制部门做本职工作。还告诉他们，事情就这样定了。我真不明白那些写这些东西、同意这些东西并在此签字的人，晚上怎么能睡得着。我就是不理解。怎么能这么做？作为工程师，我觉得这应受谴责。作为乘客，你对此有何感受？哦，是的。是的，我不会乘坐787。

cues.en: That just makes, you know, because I've been kind of avoiding flying on a 787, and seeing this, I would definitely avoid flying on a 787. In part two, inside a Boeing 787 plant, workers reveal they fear to fly the plane they built. If the Dreamliner represents Boeing's future, then I've come to the place where that future will be built, in this assembly plant in Charleston, South Carolina.
cues.zh: 这就说明了，你知道，因为我一直有点避免乘坐787，看到这个，我肯定会避免乘坐787。在第二部分，走进波音787工厂内部，工人们透露他们害怕乘坐自己制造的飞机。如果梦想客机代表波音的未来，那么我来到了这个未来将被建造的地方，位于南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿的这个装配厂。

cues.en: I've been called to a meeting with a man who works inside the plant. He's taking a huge risk, even talking to me. It's been eating me alive to know what I know and to have no avenue, no venue to say anything. At his request, we used a different voice. 300 souls on the plane. Their lives, it's bigger than me. We had seen reports of bad workmanship in the plant.
cues.zh: 我被叫去与工厂内部的一名男子会面。他甚至和我说话都冒着巨大风险。知道我所知道的事情，却没有任何途径、没有任何场合说出来，这让我备受煎熬。应他的要求，我们用了不同的声音。飞机上有300条生命。他们的生命，这比我更重要。我们曾看到关于工厂工艺质量差的报道。

cues.en: But the man claimed the problems go far deeper. With all the problems reported on the 787, there's 90% that's getting swept away. Hushed up. It's an iceberg. The people that actually work on it are the biggest problem. There is an uneducated, underskilled, and uncaring staff that are building these planes, and I'm not the only one that feels that way. And he was prepared to prove it. Wearing a camera inside the plant...
cues.zh: 但这位男士声称问题远比这严重得多。787上报告的所有问题中，有90%都被掩盖了。被隐瞒了。这只是冰山一角。真正参与制造的人才是最大的问题。是那些没受过多少教育、技能不足、又毫不在乎的员工在造这些飞机，而且不止我一个人这么觉得。而他准备证明这一点。他带着摄像头进入工厂……

cues.en: to record what some workers said about the Dreamliner. You can't have somebody from McDonald's do heart surgery. That's trusting someone with your life. That's what we're doing here. I've seen a lot of things that should not go on at an airplane plant. People talking about doing drugs, looking for drugs.
cues.zh: 记录一些工人对梦想客机的说法。你不能让麦当劳的人来做心脏手术。那是把命交到别人手里。而我们这里干的正是这种事。我见过很多在飞机工厂里不该发生的事。人们谈论吸毒、找毒品。

cues.en: I have never seen anybody or heard of anybody having to take a random urinalysis. As far as I know, random drug tests just don't happen. I know they don't. Do they? You know for a fact.
cues.zh: 我从未见过或听说过有人必须接受随机尿检。据我所知，随机药检根本不存在。我知道它们不存在。对吧？你确定吗。

cues.en: When Boeing first announced the 787 back in 2003, nobody ever dreamt it would have been assembled anywhere but Washington State. The one place Boeing had always made its commercial aircraft. But new Boeing was playing by new rules. So it did something it had never done before. auctioned off final assembly to the highest bidder. They were going to hold a competition for it.
cues.zh: 2003年波音首次公布787时，没人想过它会在华盛顿州以外的地方组装。那是波音一直制造商用飞机的唯一地方。但新波音玩的是新规则。于是它做了以前从未做过的事。把总装权拍卖给出价最高者。他们要为此举办一场竞赛。

cues.en: a state against state nationwide competition, where to build this plan. I ran to my editor after I put the phone down. I think it was five o'clock. And I said, you're not going to believe this. They're not necessarily going to build it here. Washington state won, but only by giving Boeing what was then a record $3 billion in tax breaks. Five years later, Boeing's machinists walked off the job.
cues.zh: 一场州与州之间的全国竞赛，决定在哪里造这架飞机。我放下电话就冲到编辑那儿。我记得当时是五点钟。我说，你不会相信的。他们不一定会在这里造了。华盛顿州赢了，但代价是给波音当时创纪录的30亿美元税收减免。五年后，波音的机械师们罢工离岗了。

cues.en: after contract negotiations stalled. The strike cost Boeing billions and added to the Dreamliner's delays. Boeing stock was in freefall amid a global economic crisis. That strike really enraged the top executives of Boeing. And so early in 2009, they made it very clear that they wanted a second assembly line somewhere else. That turned out to be South Carolina.
cues.zh: 合同谈判陷入僵局后。这次罢工让 Boeing 损失了数十亿美元，并进一步加剧了 Dreamliner 的延期交付。在全球经济危机的笼罩下，Boeing 的股价一路暴跌。那次罢工彻底激怒了 Boeing 的高层。于是在2009年初，他们明确表示要在其他地方建第二条总装线。最终选址在了 South Carolina。

cues.en: The state offered cheap land and labor, close to $1 billion in support and no unions. The decision to build the second 787 assembly line in Charleston, South Carolina, was made because of the strike in 2008. They wanted to do it there because they wanted to weaken the union, and they did.
cues.zh: 该州提供了廉价的土地和劳动力、近10亿美元的扶持资金，而且没有工会。在 South Carolina 州的 Charleston 建立第二条 787 总装线的决定，完全是因2008年的罢工而起。他们选择在那里建厂，就是为了削弱工会，他们也确实做到了。

cues.en: It kind of has a shameless feel to it, right? It's very manipulative and not very hometown. It's not the way you treat your people in your community, unless they're not in your community, unless you see them as a source of gains to be extracted. But for Boeing, leaving behind a world-class union workforce for the greener pastures of a non-union Charleston would come at a price. Working the plant is significantly behind schedule.
cues.zh: 这让人觉得有点不择手段，对吧？极具操纵性，毫无本土情怀。你绝不会这样对待自己社区里的人，除非他们根本不算自己人，除非你只把他们当作榨取利润的对象。但对 Boeing 而言，放弃世界顶尖的工会员工队伍，转投没有工会的 Charleston 这片“沃土”，注定要付出代价。该工厂的进度严重滞后，

cues.en: and plagued by production errors. I know of one customer. They'll no longer accept planes from Charleston due to quality issues. They will only accept final assembly done in Everett, Washington. Every day when you go to work, not only are you doing your job, but you're looking at the previous job to see if someone has messed something else up on that and chose not to tell anyone. To be sure everything is done correctly and the plane is safe, Boeing has quality assurance inspectors painstakingly check
cues.zh: 而且饱受生产缺陷的困扰。我知道有一家客户，由于质量问题，他们不再接收由 Charleston 交付的飞机。他们只接收在 Washington 州 Everett 完成最终总装的飞机。每天去上班，你不仅要做好自己的工作，还得盯紧前一道工序，看是否有人搞砸了什么却选择瞒报。为了确保每道工序准确无误并保证飞机安全，Boeing 设立了质检员去严格检查

cues.en: every step of the work. But in South Carolina, this inspector says he only signs off on finished jobs. Which do you think is the priority then, schedule or quality? Schedule. If it's a constant battle between quality and schedule, we found one casualty. Hundreds of kilometers from South Carolina in Mississippi. My name is John Woods, a aerospace engineer. Worked for
cues.zh: 每一道作业流程。但在 South Carolina，这位质检员表示他只负责在完工的项目上签字验收。那你觉得哪个才是优先级，进度还是质量？当然是进度。如果质量和进度始终处于拉锯战中，我们发现了一名受害者。就在距 South Carolina 数百公里外的 Mississippi。我叫 John Woods，是一名航空航天工程师。曾就职于

cues.en: General electric, Lockheed, Boeing. John Woods spent a career in the highly specialized field of aerospace composites. Boeing hired Woods, knowing he had qualified psychiatric conditions. Attention deficit disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, and mild depression. His job was to write instructions on how to repair parts damaged during the manufacturing process. It's my job.
cues.zh: General Electric、Lockheed、Boeing。John Woods 的整个职业生涯都深耕于航空航天复合材料这一高度专业化的领域。Boeing 在明知 Woods 确诊患有精神疾病的情况下录用了他。他患有注意力缺陷障碍、强迫症以及轻度抑郁症。他的工作是编写维修指南，说明如何修复制造过程中损坏的零部件。这就是我的工作。

cues.en: to make sure that that aircraft is safe. Which says when he tried to enforce quality standards in the South Carolina plant, he was berated by his bosses. In a couple of meetings, there were several groups of managers screaming at me to dumb down my work instruction, saying you have to remove requirements from your work instructions. It's going to take too much time.
cues.zh: 确保那架飞机是安全的。他说，当他试图在南卡罗来纳工厂执行质量标准时，遭到了老板们的斥责。在几次会议上，有几组经理冲我大喊，让我简化工作指示，说必须从工作指示中删除一些要求。那会花太多时间。

cues.en: Woods says he witnessed damaged parts being ignored, papered over and hidden from view. There's no doubt the bad repair is going out the door on the 787 aircraft. I am worried that sooner or later there's going to be a structural failure on fuselage. Woods appealed to Boeing's human resources department, claiming he was being harassed for doing his job. Instead of coming to his defence...
cues.zh: 伍兹说，他亲眼目睹受损部件被无视、掩盖和藏起来不让人看到。毫无疑问，有问题的维修会随着787飞机交付出去。我担心迟早机身会出现结构性故障。伍兹向波音人力资源部门投诉，声称自己因履行职责而受到骚扰。结果部门非但没有为他辩护……

cues.en: Boeing managers put Woods under review. Weeks later, they fired him. I'll never forget this. The day before I was terminated, I was telling my brother how proud I was to be working at Boeing. It's true. So instead of saying thanks for doing a good job, because I thought I was doing what I was supposed to be doing, I had to leave in shame, really. I was embarrassed with my own family.
cues.zh: 波音的管理层反而对伍兹启动了审查。几周后，他们解雇了他。我永远不会忘记这件事。被解雇的前一天，我还在跟弟弟说，能在波音工作我有多自豪。这是真的。所以，他们没有说一句感谢我干得好，因为我以为自己是在做分内的事，结果我却不得不带着耻辱离开，真的。我在自己家人面前都感到难堪。

cues.en: He still had not lost faith in the system. He turned to the FAA, filing a whistleblower complaint. The document alleged seven serious violations in the South Carolina plant.
cues.zh: 他仍然没有对这个体系失去信心。他转向FAA，提交了一份吹哨人投诉。文件指控南卡罗来纳工厂存在七项严重违规。

cues.en: So I've gotten to the page where they reach their conclusions and their discussion, and what they found is of all the allegations. All but one of them, they could not substantiate. And the one that they could substantiate, they asked Boeing to fix it. Boeing said, okay, we fixed it. And then they closed the investigation. And that's pretty much how they all go. I mean, I've seen this so many times. Thank you. I always tell people when they call me, they call me up with information, and they say, well, I have all this information about this dangerous situation. Should I blow the whistle?
cues.zh: 我翻到了他们得出结论并进行讨论的那一页。他们发现，在所有指控当中，除了一条之外，其他的都无法证实。而那条能证实的，他们让波音去整改。波音说，好，我们改好了。然后调查就结案了。基本上每一次都是这样收场。这种情况我见过太多次了。谢谢。每当有人打电话给我，说他们掌握了一些信息，我都会告诉他们：嗯，我掌握了很多关于危险情况的资料，我该不该去举报呢？

cues.en: And I said, well, not unless you have a private trust fund or another job to go to, because you'll have a problem earning a living. I had to maximize all my credit cards to survive, to support the family. There was a lot less money for the kids, for college and everything else. It shouldn't be this hard to do the right thing. When we looked at Wood's FAA complaint, we noticed a familiar name.
cues.zh: 我的回答是，除非你有私人信托基金，或者已经找好下一份工作，否则别举报，因为你会连谋生都成问题。为了活下去、养活家人，我不得不刷爆所有信用卡。孩子的钱少了很多，上大学的钱，还有其他开销，都受影响。做正确的事不应该这么难。我们查看伍德（Wood）向美国联邦航空管理局提交的申诉时，注意到一个熟悉的名字。

cues.en: Ali Bahrami. He was the FAA's man in charge of the Dreamliner. In 2011, three years behind schedule, Boeing celebrated final approval for the 787 to fly. And it was Bahrami who signed the order. It was Bahrami who signed off on the Dreamliner batteries.
cues.zh: 阿里·巴赫拉米（Ali Bahrami）。他是美国联邦航空管理局负责“梦幻客机”的人。2011年，在推迟了三年之后，波音庆祝787机型获得最终飞行批准。签署这份命令的正是巴赫拉米。为“梦幻客机”的电池签字放行的，也是巴赫拉米。

cues.en: And after two failed, and the FAA grounded the Dreamliner, it was Bahrami who signed it back into the air. Shortly after that, he retired from the FAA. Two weeks later, Bahrami was hired as Vice President of the Aerospace Industries Association, which lobbies on behalf of Boeing. One of the first things he did was to appear before Congress to call for greater self-regulation for companies like Boeing.
cues.zh: 而在两次电池故障、美国联邦航空管理局停飞“梦幻客机”之后，又是巴赫拉米签字让它重新上天。那之后不久，他从美国联邦航空管理局退休了。仅仅两周后，巴赫拉米就被美国航空航天工业协会聘为副总裁，而这个协会正是替波音做游说的。他做的头几件事之一，就是到国会作证，呼吁给波音这类公司更大的自我监管空间。

cues.en: We urge the FAA to allow greater use of delegation, not only to take full advantage of industry expertise, but to increase the collaboration that improves aviation safety. One day you're regulating the airline and the next day you're working for it. You can't possibly be tough on the industry that you're regulating because you'll never get that plumb job after you leave.
cues.zh: 我们敦促FAA允许更多使用授权，不仅充分利用行业专业知识，还要加强合作以提升航空安全。今天你在监管航空公司，明天你就在为其工作。你不可能对正在监管的行业强硬，因为离职后你永远得不到那份肥差。

cues.en: The regulators at the FAA will rarely cross Boeing. They simply won't. It's the Washington influence game and Boeing is a master. Last year the company had over a hundred registered lobbyists. 78 of them were former government workers. Three were former members of Congress. Boeing chief executive Jim McNerney is chairman of President Obama's Export Council. The president's former chief of staff came from Boeing's board.
cues.zh: FAA的监管者很少敢跟波音对着干，他们根本不会。这就是华盛顿的影响力游戏，而波音是大师。去年公司有超过一百名注册游说者，其中78人是前政府工作人员，三人是前国会议员。波音首席执行官Jim McNerney是奥巴马总统出口委员会的主席。总统的前幕僚长来自波音董事会。

cues.en: as did his second Commerce Secretary. As Secretary of State Hillary Clinton helped broker a $3.7 billion sale of Boeing planes to a Russian airline. Even President Obama boasts that he works for Boeing. So I teased Jay every time I see him. I said, you know, I deserve a gold watch because I'm selling your stuff all the time. Jay is Jim McNerney. It's clear what Boeing gets from the US government.
cues.zh: 他的第二任商务部长也是如此。作为国务卿，希拉里·克林顿帮助促成了一笔37亿美元的波音飞机销售给一家俄罗斯航空公司。甚至奥巴马总统都吹嘘他为波音工作。所以每次见到Jay我都调侃他，我说，你知道吗，我该得一块金表，因为我一直在推销你的东西。Jay就是Jim McNerney。波音从美国政府得到什么很清楚。

cues.en: What's not so clear is what it gives back. Boeing paid no taxes in 2013, no federal income taxes. That's not a unique year. Over the last 12 years, they claimed over $1.6 billion in federal tax refunds, even though they reported $43 billion in US profits. $43 billion in profit, but none of that comes from the Dreamliner, which has cost billions and is years away from making money.
cues.zh: 不那么清楚的是它回馈了什么。波音2013年没交税，没交联邦所得税。这不是唯一一年。过去12年里，他们申报了超过16亿美元的联邦退税，尽管报告了430亿美元的美国利润。430亿美元利润，但没有一分来自Dreamliner，它已耗资数十亿，还需多年才能盈利。

cues.en: All of Boeing's commercial profit comes from older aircraft. Those created prior to the Dreamliner, prior to Jim McNerney, and prior to the merger. It has been the top executives and largest stockholders who have benefited most. Boeing CEO Jim McNerney made $27.5 million in 2012. That was enough to pay the salaries of the President of the United States, the Vice President.
cues.zh: 波音所有商业利润都来自 older aircraft。那些在 Dreamliner 之前、在 Jim McNerney 之前、在合并之前制造的飞机。受益最多的是高层管理者和最大股东。波音 CEO Jim McNerney 2012 年赚了 2750 万美元。这足够支付美国总统、副总统的薪水。

cues.en: The 15 cabinet secretaries, the nine Supreme Court justices, seven Joint Chiefs of Staff, and all 100 US senators. McNerney is set to retire with a pension of close to $250,000 a month. Just before Christmas 2013, Boeing demanded pension cuts from its union machinists. For Jim McNerney to be earning a pension at approximately a quarter million dollars per month.
cues.zh: 15 位内阁部长、9 位最高法院大法官、7 位参谋长联席会议成员，以及全部 100 位美国参议员。McNerney 即将退休，养老金接近每月 25 万美元。就在 2013 年圣诞节前，波音要求其工会机械师削减养老金。而 Jim McNerney 却能拿到大约每月 25 万美元的养老金。

cues.en: and think that it's okay for him to take my $2,200 a month pension is outrageous. It's absolutely outrageous. Back in South Carolina, our unauthorized tour with Boeing's new workforce is coming to a close. There's only one question left to ask.
cues.zh: 还觉得他拿走我每月 2200 美元养老金没问题，这太离谱了。绝对离谱。回到南卡罗来纳州，我们对波音新劳动力的未经授权参观即将结束。还剩一个问题要问。

cues.en: Our source asked 15 of his co-workers if they'd fly on the Dreamliner. Ten said no. Why weren't you? Why weren't you? Because I see the quality. Hi Mr. Loftus, Willjaw. That's all Will? Willjaw. Workers who fear to fly the plane they build. Quality process apparently loosened to speed up schedule.
cues.zh: 我们的消息源问了 15 位同事是否愿意乘坐 Dreamliner。10 人说不愿意。你为什么不愿意？你为什么不愿意？因为我看到了质量。你好，Loftus 先生，Willjaw。就这些吗，Will？Willjaw。工人们害怕乘坐自己造的飞机。质量流程显然被放宽以加快进度。

cues.en: Workers fired after making safety allegations. We needed answers from Boeing. Right now we're at a very exciting point in time. We have brought our production rates up to 10 airplanes a month, faster than any airplane in aviation history and to the highest level of any wide-body airplane in aviation history. There's a couple of documents I want to show you here.
cues.zh: 工人因提出安全指控后被解雇。我们需要波音给出答案。现在我们正处于一个非常激动人心的时刻。我们把生产速率提高到了每月 10 架飞机，比航空史上任何飞机都快，也达到了航空史上任何宽体飞机的最高水平。这里有几份文件我想给你们看。

cues.en: I showed him the documents suggesting Boeing had changed quality procedures and overruled inspectors to speed up production. Mr Loftus was not manager of the 787 programme in 2010 when the memos were written. I'm not familiar with this document. Former Boeing engineers have told us that these represent Boeing essentially putting schedule ahead of quality, shortchanging the engineering process to meet a schedule. Is that something you recognise? The number one...
cues.zh: 我给他看了这些文件，表明波音改变了质量程序，并否决了检查员的意见以加快生产。这些备忘录写于2010年，当时Loftus先生并不是787项目的经理。我对这份文件不熟悉。前波音工程师告诉我们，这些文件实质上表明波音将进度置于质量之上，为了赶上进度而在工程流程上偷工减料。这是您能认出的情况吗？我们在波音的首要...

cues.en: focus that we have at Boeing is ensuring that the continued safe airworthiness of an airplane, the integrity of the airplane, and the quality of the airplane going out. We've also heard directly from workers inside your South Carolina plant. They paint a grim picture really of things there. They say the workforce isn't up to the job. I'm extremely confident in the quality of the workforce in Boeing, South Carolina.
cues.zh: 重点是确保飞机持续安全适航、飞机的完整性以及出厂飞机的质量。我们也直接听到了你们南卡罗来纳工厂工人的声音。他们描绘了那里相当严峻的情况。他们说劳动力不胜任这项工作。我对波音南卡罗来纳劳动力的质量极其有信心。

cues.en: The Boeing workers at South Carolina don't share that confidence. Here's what some of them said. And then Boeing's communications director stopped the interview.
cues.zh: 南卡罗来纳的波音工人并不认同这种信心。以下是他们中一些人的说法。然后波音的传播总监中止了采访。

cues.en: So, who are these employees that you're speaking to in South Carolina that are making these points? Obviously, I can't tell you who the employees are, but they are Boeing workers who assemble the planes that you build. Well, I'm not sure it's appropriate here and now. Well, I'm assuming the buck stops with the Boeing commercial airplanes management, and so the most senior managers are the ones to answer this. We're here with the head of the 787 program.
cues.zh: 那么，你在南卡罗来纳交谈的这些提出这些观点的员工是谁？显然，我不能告诉您这些员工是谁，但他们是组装你们建造的飞机的波音工人。嗯，我不确定现在在这里是否合适。嗯，我假设最终责任在波音商用飞机管理层，所以最高级的管理者才是回答这个问题的人。我们这里请到了787项目的负责人。

cues.en: And we have these things that you need to hear, and you need to provide a response to. We have not had a chance to review this, or craft a proper response. Sorry. Step back for a second. OK. But as I do, I have the highest degree of confidence in the production system we have with the employees we have at the Boeing Company and our supply chain. Thanks.
cues.zh: 我们有些事需要听取你的意见，也需要你作出回应。我们还没来得及审阅这些内容，或者拟定一个合适的回复。抱歉。先退一步想想。好。但正因如此，我对波音公司的生产体系、我们的员工以及我们的供应链抱有最高的信心。谢谢。

cues.en: Boeing answered our questions in writing, denying it compromises safety or quality. It said our interview was hostile, unprofessional and in the worst traditions of tabloid-style television news. The company said it was confident that its battery fix prevents failures. Boeing says it uses one common FAA-approved quality system for the 787 in Everett and Charleston. Boeing noted its memo stated it did not signify authorization
cues.zh: 波音以书面形式回答了我们的问题，否认其损害了安全性或质量。它表示我们的采访充满敌意、不专业，是最糟糕的小报式电视新闻作风。该公司表示，它确信其电池修复方案能防止故障。波音称，其在埃弗里特和查尔斯顿的787采用同一套经FAA批准的质量体系。波音指出，其备忘录表明这并不意味着授权

cues.en: to ship parts that don't meet quality requirements. Boeing said it drug tests in line with company policy and applicable law. The company denies any customer has said they will only take planes from Everett. As for John Woods, Boeing says his safety claims have no merit. Toronto, May 18, 2014. Air Canada celebrates the delivery of its first 787. This is the modern marketing reality of the Dreamliner.
cues.zh: 交付不符合质量要求的零件。波音表示，其药物检测符合公司政策和适用法律。该公司否认有任何客户说过只接收来自埃弗里特的飞机。至于John Woods，波音称其安全指控毫无依据。多伦多，2014年5月18日。加拿大航空庆祝其首架787交付。这就是梦想客机在现代营销中的现实。

cues.en: Today represents a huge milestone for Air Canada. We've been waiting a long time for this airplane. It's going to allow us to grow in unprecedented ways.
cues.zh: 今天对加拿大航空来说是一个巨大的里程碑。我们为这架飞机等了很久。它将让我们以前所未有的方式实现增长。

cues.en: Because when you were eating before, where'd you put your iPad? I think our passengers are going to be very receptive of some of the new amenities. I just want to see how hard it goes back. The windows are huge. We were just excited because we really genuinely love this aircraft. Is there anything else you want to add? No, we're very, very happy. From a seating point of view, how is it different? Are there more restrooms? But is there another reality? One revealed by a burning battery.
cues.zh: 因为你之前吃东西的时候，把iPad放哪儿了？我觉得乘客们会很喜欢这些新设施。我只想看看它能往后靠多少。窗户很大。我们当时很兴奋，因为我们是真心喜欢这架飞机。你还有什么想补充的吗？没有，我们非常非常满意。从座位角度来看，有什么不同？洗手间更多了吗？但还有另一个现实吗？一个被燃烧的电池揭示出来的现实。

cues.en: by the words of the workers who build the planes. By Boeing's apparent changes to its own quality protocol. Boeing says the 787 has no more problems than previous models. The FAA says there's never been a safer time to fly. The Dreamliner is the fastest selling plane in the world. One day we may all find ourselves on board. When we do...
cues.zh: 由建造飞机的工人亲口说出。由波音明显修改了自己的质量协议揭示出来。波音说787的问题并不比之前的机型多。FAA说现在坐飞机比以前任何时候都安全。梦想客机是全球卖得最快的飞机。总有一天我们可能都会坐上它。到那时……

cues.en: We will trust Boeing has put quality first. We will trust the regulators have been rigorous. Ultimately, we will trust the plane is safe.
cues.zh: 我们会相信波音把质量放在第一位。我们会相信监管机构一直严格把关。最终，我们会相信这架飞机是安全的。
